skill.name: infsh-cli
skill.description: Use the inference.sh CLI to discover and run hosted AI apps for image, video, text, search, audio, 3D, and Twitter/X workflows.
skill.summary: CLI guidance for running hosted inference.sh AI apps with belt.
skill.author: inference-sh-skills

security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate documentation for the inference.sh CLI, but it includes remote installer commands that pipe downloaded content to a shell and a dynamic download command substitution. Most Markdown backtick, API-key placeholder, hidden-path, and documentation-link findings are false positives. Additional contextual risk comes from automatic local file uploads and Twitter/X account automation.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pipe-to-shell instructions with package-manager installation, pinned release downloads, or a reviewable script download followed by checksum and signature verification.

remediation.issue: Manual install uses dynamic command substitution to select a binary URL.
remediation.suggestion: Publish direct version-pinned artifact links and avoid shell substitutions that fetch and parse remote manifests during installation.

remediation.issue: Local file paths can be uploaded automatically to hosted apps.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit approval steps before uploading local files, and document that prompts and media leave the local machine.

remediation.issue: Twitter/X workflows can perform account-changing actions.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation of the account, target action, final text, and media before any post, DM, follow, like, or retweet command runs.

remediation.issue: Related skill installation examples use npx commands.
remediation.suggestion: Move optional skill installation to a separate manual section and warn users to review source and trust before installing additional skills.

content.user_title: Run inference.sh AI Apps from the CLI
content.value_statement: Teams need a consistent way to run hosted AI apps without managing GPUs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through CLI setup, app discovery, execution, and task tracking.
actual_capabilities: Guide installation and login for the inference.sh CLI using belt.
Discover hosted apps by list, search, category, featured status, and newest order.
Run hosted apps with inline inputs or saved input files.
Use local media paths when supported by app inputs.
Track long-running tasks, fetch results, and save outputs.
Reference examples for image, video, LLM, search, 3D, and Twitter/X app categories.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and a valid authenticated account.
Commands send prompts, inputs, and uploaded files to external inference.sh services.
Results depend on app availability, account quotas, and selected model behavior.
Twitter/X actions require connected credentials and explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Prototype Hosted AI Features
use_cases.description: Find and run image, video, text, or search apps before adding model calls to a product workflow.

use_cases.title: Generate Media Assets
use_cases.description: Run image, video, audio, upscaling, and 3D apps from a repeatable command workflow.

use_cases.title: Automate Cloud Inference Tasks
use_cases.description: Create samples, submit long jobs, check task status, and save outputs for operations scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Starter App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to find inference.sh apps for [task]. List safe options, explain the categories, and do not run anything yet.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Generation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to run [app name] with this prompt: [prompt]. Show the command first and wait for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Process Local Media
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli with [local file path] for [target app]. Confirm the exact file path and upload destination before running.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Step Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an inference.sh workflow that discovers apps, creates sample input, runs the selected app, tracks the task, and saves the result.

output_examples.input: Find an image model for a quick product mockup.
output_examples.output: Suggested FLUX and SDXL options, explained speed and quality tradeoffs, and stopped before running a paid task.

output_examples.input: Run a video generation job and check it later.
output_examples.output: Prepared a sample input, submitted the task after approval, returned the task ID, and described how to fetch the final result.

output_examples.input: Use a local image for upscaling.
output_examples.output: Confirmed the file path, warned that the image would upload to inference.sh, then ran the selected upscaler after approval.

best_practices: Inspect remote installer commands and checksums before installing the CLI.
Get explicit approval before uploading local files or running paid model jobs.
Keep API keys in environment or secret storage, not in shared prompts or logs.
anti_patterns: Pipe a remote installer into a shell without inspecting or pinning it.
Upload private local files by path without confirming the exact file.
Use Twitter/X automation without approving the account, action, and final text.

faq.question: Does this skill install inference.sh automatically?
faq.answer: It provides installation guidance, but users should inspect installer commands and approve execution before the CLI is installed.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Authenticated use requires browser login or INFSH_API_KEY for scripts and CI.

faq.question: Can it access local files?
faq.answer: It can guide commands that upload local file paths when an app accepts media inputs. Confirm paths before running.

faq.question: Can it post to Twitter/X?
faq.answer: The referenced apps include Twitter/X posting and engagement actions. Require explicit approval before any account-changing command.

faq.question: Does it run models locally?
faq.answer: No. The CLI runs hosted apps through inference.sh, so prompts and files may leave the local machine.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
